message.content: {"bid_amount":3,"public_message":"Three.","private_thought":"Win Short Line under $100 and mortgage it before the roll: mortgage value $100, so any win \u2264$99 is net cash and widens the Park 3h $1100 cushion. p2 can still raise a $200 dark-blue house via Kentucky/Illinois mortgages, so draining them here does not stop the kill house \u2014 the +liquidity is the prize. Keep raising to $99; drop at $100+."}
message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on SHORT_LINE in the current auction.

The minimum bid is $3. I will bid $1 to force p2 to pay roughly $100 for the property instead of receiving it free. I plan to mortgage Short Line before rolling if I win it under $100.

I will bid incrementally to $99 rather than jumping high. I also need to verify whether Short Line can collect rent while Reading and Pennsylvania remain mortgaged.

Mortgaged railroads do not count toward rent multipliers, so Short Line alone would collect $25. Buying it for under $100 and mortgaging immediately returns $100, netting a $97 profit at a $3 bid. p2 has $225 cash, but they would need to pay $110 to unmortgage B&O if they acquire Short Line.

A $99 bid leaves p2 with $126. They need $200 to build a fourth house on Park Place, so they cannot afford that upgrade immediately.

p2 has $225 cash. They can buy one $200 house now and have $25 left. If I force them to pay $100 for Short Line, they would have $125. That is too little to buy the $200 fourth house on Park Place. I am now checking their other mortgageable properties to see if they can raise enough cash.

Unbuilt properties can be mortgaged to raise cash. Kentucky and Illinois are unmortgaged and worth $110 and $100 respectively. p2 could mortgage one of them to cover the $100 Short Line bid and still afford a $200 house.

Mortgaging Kentucky or Illinois would give p2 enough cash to buy a house even after paying $100 for Short Line. The auction cannot drain them below house-buying capacity. I will bid up to $99 anyway.

I am calculating the exact rent values for Park Place and Boardwalk to assess the risk of landing there. From Water Works, I would need to roll a 9 to reach Park Place or an 11 to reach Boardwalk.

Rolling an 8 from Water Works lands on a Chance card, which can advance directly to Boardwalk. The probability of landing on Park Place is 4/36 and on Boardwalk is 2/36. I am now tallying my liquid assets: $546 cash plus States ($70), Ventnor ($130), and ten houses sold at half value ($25 each) equals $250 in non-Light Blue deeds. Full liquidation including Light Blue deeds would bring total cash to roughly $996.

Full liquidation totals roughly $1146. That is below the $1400 Boardwalk rent, so Boardwalk is fatal. Park Place at $1100 is survivable if almost everything is mortgaged, leaving only about $46. Winning Short Line for $3 and mortgaging it would raise cash to $643 and total liquidation to $1243. Even then, Boardwalk remains fatal.

Even with Short Line mortgaged, I would still need to mortgage a Light Blue property to survive Park Place. The net cash gain from winning at $99 is only $1, but that is better than letting p2 acquire the property for free. I will bid $3 now and raise incrementally.

I will bid $3 and raise incrementally. Forcing p2 to pay $100 would not stop them from building a house, since they can mortgage other properties for the difference. The real value is winning Short Line cheap so I can mortgage it and gain roughly $97 in cash. That extra cushion is more useful than draining their bank.

p2 may raise the bid to about $99 to prevent me from gaining roughly $97 in net cash. Short Line alone is worth only $25 in rent and $100 mortgaged, so buying it above $100 offers little value unless paired with B&O. They might be trying to deny that liquidity gain entirely.

p2 now holds the full red monopoly with Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois. Indiana is mortgaged. They also own Marvin Gardens and the yellow set. I will bid $3 on Short Line and raise to $99 if p2 tries to block me.
